parentReviewCorrectionPass.finding: Parent review of the first result-shape pass found normalizeResultCases returned without a resultSchemaError in two cases it should have flagged: (1) a file object that omitted `assertionResults` entirely (undefined) was silently tolerated (`if (assertionResultsRaw === undefined) return`), and (2) a case object whose `status` was missing, null, non-string, or an empty string was pushed into `cases` with no schema error recorded at all. This contradicted the function's own stated contract (and the doc comment, which already claimed missing/malformed assertionResults was flagged) even though classifyExecution's independent, pre-existing per-case status check still correctly forced setup_block downstream -- the diagnostic just wasn't structured/attributable at the normalizeResultCases layer.
fix: Removed the special-cased `if (assertionResultsRaw === undefined) return` early exit; a missing assertionResults now falls into the same `!Array.isArray(assertionResultsRaw)` branch as any other non-array value, with a reason distinguishing 'is missing' (when actually undefined) from 'is not an array' (any other non-array value, e.g. `{}`) so the two remain separately greppable while sharing one code path.

Added an explicit `isValidStatus(value) => typeof value === 'string' && value.length > 0` check on every valid case object; a missing/null/non-string/empty status now records a resultSchemaError with reason `...status is missing or invalid` and a `{ type, value? }` detail (the raw string value is included only when the status IS a string, so an empty string is distinguishable from 'no status at all' or a wrong type).

The case is still pushed into `cases` with its raw status preserved (not nulled out) in both the missing-assertionResults-tolerant-before and invalid-status paths, so no safe raw evidence is dropped -- only the file-level assertionResults-missing/non-array case and the case-level null/non-object case (both pre-existing behavior, unchanged) skip pushing a case, and the latter still substitutes a safe all-null placeholder as before.
classifyExecution, runExecute, parseResultsFile, and every other prior gate/behavior are unchanged in this pass -- only normalizeResultCases's internal validation was tightened.
parentReviewCorrectionPass.verification: The one pre-existing test that asserted the now-corrected (wrong) tolerant behavior -- 'tolerates a case missing its required status field as no schema error' -- was updated to assert the corrected behavior (resultSchemaError now set, case still preserved) and retitled to note the correction. No other existing test's expected outcome changed.

boundedDefect.description: runExecute built the per-case list with `(results?.testResults ?? []).flatMap(file => (file.assertionResults ?? []).map(testCase => ({ ...testCase.status, ... })))` before assembling raw process evidence. Valid, successfully-parsed JSON with a wrong shape -- `testResults` as a non-array (e.g. an object), a null entry inside `testResults`, `assertionResults` as a non-array, or a null entry inside `assertionResults` -- would throw a TypeError (`.flatMap`/`.map` is not a function on a non-array, or 'Cannot read properties of null') instead of producing a diagnosed setup_block. Separately, `parseResultsFile`'s `readFileSync(resultsPath, 'utf8')` call was outside its try/catch, so a filesystem-read failure on an existing-but-unreadable path (e.g. a directory) would escape as an unstructured, uncaught error instead of becoming structured evidence alongside the existing JSON-parse diagnostic.
boundedDefect.riskWithoutFix: A malformed-but-successfully-parsed Vitest reporter output, or a results path that exists but cannot be read, could crash runExecute with an unhandled exception instead of producing a report at all -- the opposite of the fail-closed, always-diagnosable contract the runner is supposed to guarantee.

fix.parseResultsFile: Split into two independent try/catches: the `readFileSync` call is now wrapped and failures become a `resultsReadError: { message, code, path }`, distinct and mutually exclusive from the pre-existing `resultsParseError` (a `JSON.parse` failure on bytes that were read successfully). A missing file still yields all three (`results`, `resultsReadError`, `resultsParseError`) null.
fix.normalizeResultCases: Pure function (not a test-only reimplementation -- runExecute calls this exact function) that walks parsed `results.testResults` -> per-file `assertionResults` -> per-case entries, validating each level's shape before touching it: a missing/non-array `testResults`, a null/non-object file entry, a missing/null/non-array `assertionResults`, a null/non-object case entry, or a case whose `status` is missing/null/non-string/empty are each recorded as a single structured `resultSchemaError` (the first one encountered, with a human-readable `reason` and a `{ type, value? }` detail) instead of throwing. A null/malformed case entry is replaced with a safe all-null placeholder case; a case with an invalid status is still pushed with its raw status preserved. The returned `cases` array is always a plain array of plain objects, never containing `null`. See parentReviewCorrectionPass above for the fix to the missing-assertionResults/invalid-status gap found by parent review.
fix.classifyExecution: Gained two new early gates, `if (execution.resultsReadError) return 'setup_block'` and `if (execution.resultSchemaError) return 'setup_block'`, placed alongside the pre-existing `resultsParseError` gate. Existing gates, the count/denominator/pending-todo/per-case checks, and the source_pass/source_behavioral_failure split are all unchanged.
fix.runExecute: Now calls `const { results, resultsReadError, resultsParseError } = parseResultsFile(resultsPath)` followed by `const { cases, resultSchemaError } = normalizeResultCases(results)`, replacing the inline `.flatMap`/`.map` chain entirely. The `execution` object and the `--execute` JSON report both gained `resultsReadError` and `resultSchemaError` fields (mirroring the existing `resultsParseError` field), each null unless its specific failure occurred. Raw spawn evidence (`report.spawn`), raw counts (`report.rawCounts`), and the full per-case list (`report.cases`) are unchanged in shape and are still populated whenever the underlying data allows it, independent of classification.
fix.noDuplication: cli-contract.test.mjs imports and calls the real, exported normalizeResultCases/parseResultsFile/classifyExecution -- it does not reimplement any normalization or classification logic for testing.

notExecuted.note: The costly real UI baseline (--execute against the pinned Drogon-mentu-session source, spawning the real Vitest suite) was not rerun as part of this review. The frozen evidence.json (source_behavioral_failure, 6 passed / 2 failed of 8) is unchanged and remains the admitted execute-mode evidence. Its shape is compatible with the new report.resultsReadError/report.resultSchemaError fields, which would simply add two more null-valued fields alongside the already-recorded exitCode/signal/resultsParseError on a future rerun, since that admitted run's results.json was well-formed.

limitations: This is result-shape/normalization hardening only, never a candidate parity result or a re-run of the admitted evidence.json baseline.

The wiring tests exercise the real parseResultsFile/normalizeResultCases/classifyExecution chain against real throwaway fixture files, but do not spawn a real vitest process; the spawnSync/staging portions of runExecute are unchanged and remain covered only by the frozen evidence.json admitted run plus the pre-existing spawn-evidence unit tests (signal/timeout/spawnError) against hand-built execution objects.

normalizeResultCases records only the first schema problem encountered per call (problems[0]) rather than an exhaustive list, matching the existing single-shot diagnostic style of resultsParseError/resultsReadError.
